summary_of_change:
In operational reality reflected in 2025 and early 2026 financial results, L3Harris is executing with strong unit volume demand across its core military franchise. In its latest quarterly results for fiscal 2025, the company delivered $5,881.0M in revenue, supporting an annualized run-rate of $23,524.0M and delivering year-over-year revenue growth of 7.3%. Gross margin stood firm at 25.5%, while adjusted segment operating margins held consistent across 2025 results at 15.7% to 15.9%. Operating performance is driven by the ongoing LHX NeXt operational efficiency initiative, which continues to strip structural costs out of integrated prime manufacturing facilities heading into 2026.

Unit-level demand metrics demonstrate robust defense customer commitment. LHX concluded 2025 with a record funded defense and space backlog exceeding $40.7B, supported by trailing book-to-bill order ratios fluctuating between 1.2x and 1.4x into 2026. The 2025 and 2026 operational cadence has seen organic order flow surges in tactical communications, resilient night vision platforms, space-based early missile tracking architectures, and advanced solid rocket motor production inside the Missile Solutions division. Despite negative EAC adjustments on isolated legacy contracts, demand for sovereign electronic warfare and resilient space hardware remains at historical highs.

Cash flow conversion remains resilient in 2025/2026 results. Full-year free cash flow guidance stands near $3.0B, reflecting normalized conversion of DoD receivables following temporary payment milestone shifts. Management has maintained disciplined capital allocation, pausing speculative share buybacks to concentrate surplus operating cash flow on gross debt paydown and targeted capacity expansion across missile propulsion facilities.

market_pricing_in:
At the current market price of $234.72, L3Harris Technologies trades at 16.3x normalized Owner Earnings and 19.8x EV/OE, reflecting substantial skepticism from institutional investors. The market is pricing in severe governance turbulence following the abrupt termination of Chairman and CEO Christopher Kubasik over an internal code-of-conduct investigation. This leadership disruption has triggered legal scrutiny from shareholder litigation firms, executive stability concerns, and rating downgrades from prominent sell-side desks. Investors fear that internal management distractions will derail program execution across multi-year Department of Defense initiatives.

Beyond boardroom disruption, Mr. Market is treating current defense industry cash flows with caution due to persistent supply chain friction, unfavorable Estimate-at-Completion (EAC) contract adjustments in the Missile Solutions segment, and delayed monetization catalysts, such as the postponement of the Missile Solutions business public carve-out to mid-2027. Rather than pricing structural franchise collapse, the market is discounting LHX for execution slippage and sticky corporate debt (-$50.61 per share of net balance sheet obligations) accumulated during aggressive merger integration. The resulting multiple reflects skepticism that operating leverage can overcome rising program demonstration costs and integration drag.
